overview.description: Pelmanism is a simple memory game in which players turn over two cards at a time from a face-down layout to find matching pairs. Also known as Concentration or Memory; in Japan as Shinkei-suijaku. The British name comes from the Pelman Institute (London, 1899).

history.origins: The name Pelmanism comes from Britain: Christopher Louis Pelman founded the Pelman Institute for the Scientific Development of Mind, Memory and Personality in London in 1899. The game is a simple memory pastime also known as Concentration or Memory (English) and Shinkei-suijaku in Japan.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

setup.equipment: Standard 52-card deck, table or floor space. Cards are spread face down and must not overlap.
setup.dealing: No cards are dealt to hands. All cards are thoroughly shuffled and spread face down on the playing surface in a regular pattern or irregular layout; positions are fixed for the round.

rules.objective: Score the most points by collecting matching pairs. On your turn you turn two cards face up; if they match (same rank, suits ignored), you keep the pair and take another turn; if not, you turn them face down again and the turn passes.
rules.gameplay:
1. Preparation: Shuffle the deck and spread all cards face down so they do not overlap.
2. Play: Players take turns. At your turn, turn face up any two cards from the layout. If they match (same denomination), take both cards and place them in front of you, and take another turn. If they do not match, turn them face down in place and the next player plays.
3. Matching: With a 52-card pack, cards match if they have the same rank (e.g. two sixes, two kings); suits are ignored. There are 26 pairs.
4. End: Play continues until every card has been taken as part of a pair. Each player scores one point per pair collected; the player with the most points wins (ties share the win).
keyRules: Turn exactly two cards face up per turn.
Match is by rank (denomination) only; suits do not matter.
If the two cards match, take them and take another turn.
If they do not match, turn them face down again in the same positions and pass the turn.
Winner is the player with the most pairs when the layout is empty; ties all win.

strategy.basic: Remember where you have seen each rank. When you turn a card, note its position and rank so you can match it later.
strategy.intermediate: Track which cards have been shown and turned back; prioritise turning a card when you already know the position of its pair.
strategy.advanced: Remember the full sequence of revealed cards and positions; minimise information given to opponents when you fail to match.
tips: Fix the layout pattern in memory (e.g. row and column) to recall positions.
When you see a pair, take it immediately to get an extra turn.

list.name: Match by rank and colour
list.description: When using only two cards of each type (e.g. from a standard pack), players may agree that cards match only if they have the same denomination and the same colour (e.g. both red or both black), making matching harder.
list.emptyOverridesReason: No engine overrides; rule change only.

list.name: Four of each type
list.description: Some packs have four identical cards of each type instead of two, so the first card of a new rank has three possible pairings and the start is easier; the game still gets easier as the layout shrinks.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Deck composition only; no engine overrides.

difficulty.easy: Random choice of two face-down positions; no memory.
difficulty.medium: Remember recently revealed cards and positions; prefer flipping when a matching position is known.
difficulty.hard: Full memory of all revealed cards and positions; minimise giving information on failed flips.

considerations: AI must track layout state and which cards have been seen; difficulty scales with memory and inference.

customActions.description: Turn two cards from the face-down layout face up. If they match (same rank), take the pair and take another turn; otherwise turn them face down again and pass the turn.
customActions.constraints: Exactly two cards must be chosen from the layout; both must be face down.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck; often pairs are used (e.g. two decks or 52 cards laid face down). Pelmanism is a memory game: players flip two cards at a time to find matching pairs; the full deck is used for the layout.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) with thirteen ranks each. In Pelmanism, suits and ranks define which cards form a pair; players must remember positions to match pairs.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranks Ace through King; matching in Pelmanism is usually by identical card (same suit and rank) or by rank-only pair depending on variant. Players turn two cards face up per turn to find matches.
